recap.label: Daily Recap
recap.periodEnd: Wed, Nov 11, 2026, 4:00 PM ET (that day's close)
recap.timezoneNote: All times below are shown in ET (America/New_York). Items marked headline were written only from the publisher's headline and summary.

driver.text: Per WSJ, U.S. stocks rose as CoreWeave's earnings update eased worries that AI profits would not come soon enough to cover infrastructure debt burdens (4:23 PM ET), and Nasdaq jumped after the update re-energized the AI trade (2:36 PM ET). The FT reported the Nasdaq erased last week's losses as CoreWeave's results and the prospect of a higher Anthropic IPO valuation boosted sentiment (4:04 PM ET), and Bloomberg reported the Nasdaq 100 nearly erased its losses since the U.S. midterm election as dip buyers returned (8:28 AM ET). WSJ reported European chip stocks climbed after CoreWeave's results (4:25 AM ET). On rates, WSJ reported Asian bond yields rose on growing expectations for a Fed rate hike next month after hotter-than-expected U.S. inflation data (1:37 AM ET), and gold futures settled back under $4,000 for a second session as inflation worries kept rate-hike expectations up (2:47 PM ET). WSJ reported crude futures stabilized after recent losses while the market awaited clarity on talks to end the U.S.-Iran conflict (4:27 PM ET). The U.S. Treasury market was closed for Veterans Day. Written from headlines and publisher summaries only.

cryptoDriver.text: CoinDesk reported bitcoin sat out the stock rebound as ETF outflows extended to a fourth day (6:37 AM ET), and that bitcoin barely moved on the hot CPI report as ETF selling slowed (7:19 AM ET). The Block reported stablecoin supply fell $14.2 billion, the largest contraction since the 2022 bear market, with USDT and USDC supply down nearly $11 billion over the past month (12:23 PM ET). Written from headlines and publisher summaries only.

items.headline: Baird downgrades Nvidia to Neutral from Outperform, cuts price target to $200 from $500
items.summary: Baird downgraded Nvidia to Neutral from Outperform and lowered its price target from $500 to $200, per Yahoo Finance analyst data. Nvidia closed up 2.87% on the day.

items.headline: Morgan Stanley keeps Nvidia at Overweight, maintains $300 price target
items.summary: Morgan Stanley reiterated its Overweight rating on Nvidia and maintained its $300 price target, per Yahoo Finance analyst data.

items.headline: Citigroup lowers Nvidia price target to $285 from $315, keeps Buy
items.summary: Citigroup kept its Buy rating on Nvidia and lowered its price target from $315 to $285, per Yahoo Finance analyst data.

items.headline: Wells Fargo lowers Nvidia price target to $300 from $315, keeps Overweight
items.summary: Wells Fargo kept its Overweight rating on Nvidia and lowered its price target from $315 to $300, per Yahoo Finance analyst data.

items.headline: Law Firm Wachtell Lipton to Lead Nvidia Internal Investigation
items.summary: Per WSJ, the New York law firm will lead Nvidia's internal investigation into whether the company was the target of a foreign espionage effort. Written from the headline and the publisher's summary only.

items.headline: The 31-Year-Old Trader Who Called Out Jensen Huang's 'China Problem'—and Shorted Nvidia
items.summary: Per WSJ, Culper Research published a report on Huang's 'China problem' that went largely unnoticed for six months before drawing attention this week. Written from the headline and the publisher's summary only.

items.headline: Nvidia China Scandal Demands Answers, Says Congressman
items.summary: Per Bloomberg, Rep. Raja Krishnamoorthi said Congress needs answers from CEO Jensen Huang over his reported relationship with a woman suspected of ties to Chinese intelligence, and that lawmakers could consider a subpoena if Huang does not voluntarily appear. Written from the headline and the publisher's summary only.

items.headline: Huang's Ties to Trump Under Scrutiny After Spy Claim
items.summary: Per Bloomberg, actions by the Trump administration and by Huang are coming under sharper scrutiny by Congress amid investigations into the affair Huang had with a woman alleged to be a Chinese spy. Written from the headline and the publisher's summary only.

items.headline: Nvidia is spending more than ever on Washington lobbying. It may not stop Congress from limiting China chip sales now.
items.summary: Per MarketWatch, a former U.S. ambassador to Beijing is quoted saying there is no question Congress will push for a complete ban on the sale of advanced semiconductors into China. Written from the headline and the publisher's summary only.

items.headline: Google in, but Nvidia out as US lines up Apec CEO Summit delegation: source
items.summary: Per SCMP, citing a source familiar with the arrangements, Huang is unlikely to attend next week's Apec CEO Summit in Shenzhen at this stage. Written from the headline and the publisher's summary only.

items.headline: Nvidia's Bull Case Hinges on Huang Surviving China Spy Probe
items.summary: Per Bloomberg, Nvidia's investigation of CEO Jensen Huang's affair with an alleged Chinese spy is raising questions about the company's future and sending its stock into a tailspin. Written from the headline and the publisher's summary only.

items.headline: Nvidia Scandal Tests the Resilience of the Global AI Boom
items.summary: Per WSJ, the article asks whether the AI boom could carry on without Jensen Huang, described as its biggest cheerleader. Written from the headline and the publisher's summary only.

items.summary: Per Bloomberg, Google is adding its Gemini app to Apple's CarPlay system, expanding options for drivers who may already use the assistant on their Apple devices. Alphabet (GOOG) closed up 2.0%. Written from the headline and the publisher's summary only.

items.summary: Per SCMP, representatives from Google and Boeing will be included in the U.S. business delegation at next week's Apec CEO Summit in Shenzhen, the event organiser has confirmed. Written from the headline and the publisher's summary only.

morning.label: Morning Brief
morning.timezoneNote: All times shown in ET (America/New_York). Items marked headline were written only from the publisher's headline and summary.

driver.text: Per WSJ, stocks fell Tuesday on hotter-than-expected inflation data and AI worries, and yields jumped (Nov 10, 4:54 PM and 4:17 PM ET). After the close, WSJ reported CoreWeave met Wall Street expectations with its backlog at $133 billion and shares rising (5:14 PM ET). Overnight, WSJ reported Nasdaq futures led stock futures higher as AI optimism returned (4:16 AM ET) and European chip stocks climbed after CoreWeave's results (4:25 AM ET); Bloomberg tied the rebound to demand for Anthropic's IPO (5:46 AM ET). WSJ reported Asian bond yields rose on expectations for a Fed rate hike (1:37 AM ET), the dollar reached a four-week high (4:55 AM ET), and Brent crude rose above $92 a barrel after a sharp selloff (3:02 AM ET). Written from headlines and publisher summaries only.
